title: Unbounded exchange invertibility under arbitrary coefficient restriction
statement: Let R and S be commutative rings in the coefficient universe and φ : R →+* S any ring map. For a cartesian square of schemes [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions] and K in D(X_et,S) [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories], the image under derived restriction of scalars of the S-coefficient canonical unbounded exchange [def-kun-unbounded-exchange] at K is invertible if and only if the R-coefficient exchange at the derived restriction of K is invertible. No properness, torsion, flatness, boundedness or exchange-invertibility assumption is imposed.

source.place: Tag 0D6J(3), coefficient restriction and canonical mate comparison

proof.text: Normalize the ModuleCat-coefficient exchange defined with L(g*) to the exchange defined with the exact induced functors D(g*). Expand leftDerivedUpperStarComp and derivedSquareUpperStarIso through leftDerivedUpperStarIsoMapDerivedCategory; functoriality of mapDerivedCategoryNatIso and one naturality equation identify the square transformations. Transport the mates using conjugateEquiv_mateEquiv_vcomp and mateEquiv_conjugateEquiv_vcomp. Conjugates of the invertible left-adjoint comparisons are invertible, so the two exchange components have equivalent invertibility tests. This argument does not require an additional assertion that the two derived adjunction constructions coincide.

Restriction followed by forgetting R-module structure agrees definitionally with forgetting S-module structure on sheaves. mapDerivedCategoryCompIso and mapDerivedCategoryNatIso give the corresponding natural isomorphism on unbounded derived categories. The conservativity clauses of the unbounded abelian exchange comparison for R and S, together with NatIso.isIso_map_iff for this isomorphism, show that restricting any S-derived morphism preserves and reflects its invertibility.

For each coefficient ring, use the exchange equation of the unbounded abelian exchange comparison. Its two direct-image comparisons and the inverse-image comparisons are invertible. Cancel these endpoint factors using isIso_comp_left_iff and isIso_comp_right_iff. The conservative derived forgetting functor then identifies invertibility of the exact module exchange with invertibility of the abelian exchange at its forgotten object.

Apply naturality of the abelian exchange to the component of the restriction-forgetting natural isomorphism at K. NatTrans.isIso_app_iff_of_iso identifies its invertibility at the two underlying objects. Combine this with the preceding two steps and the L-to-D normalization for R and S to obtain precisely the stated equivalence.
